title: Your right to move freely in Nigeria
summary: As a citizen you are entitled to move and travel freely throughout Nigeria and to live in any part of it, and you cannot be expelled from Nigeria or refused entry or exit.
body_plain: The Constitution guarantees freedom of movement and travel. Every citizen of Nigeria is entitled to move and travel freely throughout Nigeria and to reside in any part of it, and no citizen shall be expelled from Nigeria or refused entry or exit. This right can be limited only by laws that are reasonably justifiable in a democratic society, such as restrictions on a person reasonably suspected of a criminal offence.
rights: You may move freely throughout Nigeria and live in any part of it (s.41(1)).
As a citizen, you cannot be expelled from Nigeria or refused entry or exit (s.41(1)).
do_list: If restricted, ask on what legal basis your movement is being limited.
dont_list: Do not assume checkpoints can bar a citizen from lawful travel without legal basis.
common_situations: An official prevents you from travelling within Nigeria or leaving the country without explaining why.
Your passport or travel document is retained without a clear written process.
You are confined to an area even though you are not told that you are under arrest.
words_to_use: Am I legally required to remain here, or am I free to go?
What law or court order restricts my movement?
Please provide a receipt and written reason for retaining my travel document.
if_violated: Record the checkpoint, border point, time, officials, documents examined, and authority claimed.
Preserve tickets, passport records, notices, receipts, and proof of financial loss caused by the restriction.
Seek prompt legal advice, especially where travel is time-sensitive or a document has been retained.

citations.source_name: 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
citations.quote: Every citizen of Nigeria is entitled to move freely throughout Nigeria and to reside in any part thereof, and no citizen of Nigeria shall be expelled from Nigeria or refused entry thereby or exit therefrom.
